reason: The zero set is the preimage of the closed set \(\{0\}\) under the continuous function \(f\).
text:
Since \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\) and the continuous map \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) has closed preimages of closed sets, \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). Moreover,
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.
